notes: Seventh consecutive workday: first 8 hours at 1.5x and over 8 at 2x (Lab. Code § 510(a)); not representable in the daily_overtime params, recorded here.
No statewide minimum-rest-between-shifts or predictive-scheduling law for retail; see city files (e.g. San Francisco, Los Angeles, Berkeley, Emeryville) for local ordinances.
16-17 school-week weekly cap: Lab. Code § 1391 sets 48 h/week; a lower school-week cap may exist in the Education Code work-permit rules — not yet verified, so not encoded.
Extra param keys: rest_break.not_required_under_minutes, reporting_time_pay.max_paid_hours, minor_limits.max_hours_non_school_day, minor_limits.latest_end_before_non_school_day.
Wage Order 7 meal/rest premium: one hour of pay per workday a required rest (or meal) period is not provided.

No tip credit: 'An employer may not use an employee's tips as a credit toward its obligation to pay the minimum wage' (DIR/DLSE Minimum Wage FAQ Q8, https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/faq_minimumwage.htm; Lab. Code § 351). No tipped_minimum_wage rule: tipped employees get the full minimum wage.

Alcohol (DLSE Child Labor Laws 2013, BPC 25663/25667): under-21s may not work at all, during business hours, in the part of premises primarily used for on-premises alcohol sales (bars) except as musicians; 18-20 may serve alcohol in the food-service area of a bona fide eating place but not as bartenders (no bartender role tag; not encoded). The rule encodes under-18 alcohol_service conservatively (packaged-goods sales under constant 21+ supervision are allowed).

Minor hazardous work: California follows the federal hazardous orders (LC 1294.1 cites 29 CFR 570); its 14-15 cooking allowance (in plain sight of customers, not the sole duty) is broader than federal 570.34(c), so the stricter federal rule (federal.json) applies to FLSA-covered employers. No extra CA role bans encoded.

rules.summary: Work over 8 hours in a workday is paid at 1.5x and over 12 hours at 2x (seventh-day rules also apply).

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 510(a) — Day's work; overtime
citation.excerpt: Any work in excess of eight hours in one workday ... Any work in excess of 12 hours in one day ... no less than twice the regular rate

rules.summary: Work over 40 hours in a workweek is paid at 1.5x.

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 510(a) — Day's work; overtime
citation.excerpt: any work in excess of 40 hours in any one workweek ... shall be compensated at the rate of no less than one and one-half times

rules.summary: A 30-minute unpaid meal period is required for a work period over 5 hours; it may be waived by mutual consent if the day is no more than 6 hours.

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 512(a) — Meal periods
citation.excerpt: work period of more than five hours per day without providing the employee with a meal period of not less than 30 minutes

rules.summary: A second 30-minute meal period is required for a work period over 10 hours; waivable if no more than 12 hours and the first was not waived.

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 512(a) — Meal periods
citation.excerpt: more than 10 hours per day without providing the employee with a second meal period of not less than 30 minutes

rules.summary: Employees get a paid 10-minute rest period per 4 hours worked or major fraction thereof; none required if the day is under 3.5 hours.

citation.title: IWC Wage Order 7-2001 (Mercantile), § 12 — Rest periods
citation.excerpt: ten (10) minutes net rest time per four (4) hours or major fraction thereof

rules.summary: An employee who reports but gets less than half the scheduled day is paid for half the scheduled day, at least 2 and at most 4 hours.

citation.title: IWC Wage Order 7-2001 (Mercantile), § 5 — Reporting time pay
citation.excerpt: shall be paid for half the usual or scheduled day's work, but in no event for less than two (2) hours nor more than four (4) hours

rules.summary: California's minimum wage is $16.90 an hour for all employers from January 1, 2026.

citation.title: DIR/DLSE — Minimum Wage FAQ
citation.excerpt: the minimum wage is $16.90 per hour for all employers (effective January 1, 2026)

rules.summary: While school is in session, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 3 hours on a school day and 18 hours a week, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 1391(a)(1)-(2) — Minors' hours
citation.excerpt: while school is in session ... not more than three hours in any schoolday, nor more than 18 hours in any week

rules.summary: Minors 15 and under may work at most 8 hours a day and 40 a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (until 9 p.m. June 1 through Labor Day).

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 1391(a)(1) — Minors' hours
citation.excerpt: more than eight hours in one day of 24 hours, or more than 40 hours in one week, or before 7 a.m. or after 7 p.m.

rules.summary: While school is in session, 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 4 hours on a school day (8 otherwise), between 5 a.m. and 10 p.m. before a school day (12:30 a.m. before a non-school day).

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 1391(a)(3)-(4) — Minors' hours
citation.excerpt: while school is in session ... a minor 16 or 17 years of age for more than four hours in any schoolday

rules.summary: 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 a week, not before 5 a.m. or after 10 p.m. before a school day (12:30 a.m. before a non-school day).

citation.title: Cal. Lab. Code § 1391(a)(3) — Minors' hours
citation.excerpt: more than eight hours in one day of 24 hours or more than 48 hours in one week, or before 5 a.m., or after 10 p.m. on any day preceding a schoolday

params.exception_note: Off-premises sellers (stores) may employ minors under 18 to sell alcohol only if constantly supervised by a person 21+ (BPC 25663(b)).

rules.summary: In California only people 18 or older may serve alcohol in a restaurant (not as bartenders until 21); minors under 18 may sell packaged alcohol only under constant supervision by someone 21+.

citation.title: DIR/DLSE — Child Labor Laws (2013), Liquor and Lottery Sales (BPC 25663, 25667)
citation.excerpt: Persons 18 to 21 years of age may serve alcohol in a bona fide public eating establishment if the person is no employed as a bartender ...
